properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 5:44PM MDT until November 2 at 9:10PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Colorado...

...This is a PARTICULARY DANGEROUS SITUATION...

For the San Juan River at Pagosa Springs affecting Archuleta County.

.Significant and historic flooding is possible along the San Juan
River at Pagosa Springs. Widespread rainfall is expected to begin
early Sunday morning and continue through Monday morning. Excessive
runoff will also increase flooding risks. The region should prepare
for a dangerous and impactful flood event.

For the San Juan River...including Pagosa Springs...major flooding is
forecast. This is a particularly dangerous situation.

* WHAT...Major flooding caused by excessive rainfall is forecast
along the San Juan River. This is a Particularly Dangerous
Situation.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon to Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Portions of San Juan Street are beginning
to flood.  Waters have reached the foundation of the Colorado
Ranger Building.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 PM MDT Saturday the stage was 6.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow afternoon to a crest of 17.0 feet early Monday morning.
It will then fall below flood stage Monday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 10/05/1911.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Heed any evacuation orders from local authorities.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

The next statement will be issued Monday evening at 915 PM MST.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 31 at 8:34PM HST until October 31 at 11:45PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
FFWHFO

The National Weather Service in Honolulu has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The island of Kauai in Kauai County

* Until 1145 PM HST.

* At 834 PM HST, gauge reports indicate flooding continues on the
Hanalei River, including at and near Hanalei Bridge. Therefore,
even though heavy rain has ended, the flood warning is being
extended.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by previous heavy rain.

SOURCE...Gauges reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Areas along and near the Hanalei River, including the Hanalei
Bridge.
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 8:42PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity for the
following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent east-northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the
St John River have slowed flow at Astor. Forecast rainfall may lead
to additional rises within Moderate flood stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EDT Saturday was 3.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.7 feet
Monday evening.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 1 at 1:17AM CDT until November 1 at 1:45AM CST by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 145 AM CST.

* At 116 AM CDT, a strong thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 17 nm southwest of Empire Mica Wreck. The
severe thunderstorm was nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 1 at 1:46AM CDT until November 1 at 1:45AM CST by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
SMWMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL from 20 to
60 NM...

* Until 145 AM CST.

* At 145 AM CDT, a strong thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 29 nm south of Okaloosa Deep Water Reef, or
54 nm south of Destin, moving west at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
